mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: Continued risk for damaging wind may continue through the late afternoon/early evening

details.label: Summary
details.text: Continued risk for damaging wind may continue through the late afternoon/early evening

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Mixed mode thunderstorm activity is ongoing along and south of a surface boundary across portions of Virginia this afternoon. A cluster has developed across south-central Virginia and is moving southeastward. The environment downstream of this cluster is moderately to strongly unstable. Daytime heating has allowed temperatures to rise into the mid 90s, with steepening low-level lapse rates. Deep layer shear decreases with southward extent but it is possible that with cold pool organization, the damaging wind potential may increase as this line shifts southeastward into the favorable environment. Closer to the northern boundary within the more favorable deep layer shear, a supercell is moving south east across north-central Virginia. While deep layer shear is sufficient, low level flow is fairly week. This will likely keep the main threats to large hail and damaging wind. Watch issuance is being considered soon

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: Storms may increase out of the Panhandles and into southern Kansas through this evening. Areas of strong to damaging wind gusts will be possible

details.label: Summary
details.text: Storms may increase out of the Panhandles and into southern Kansas through this evening. Areas of strong to damaging wind gusts will be possible

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Surface observations show very hot conditions have developed, with temperatures at or above 105 F from the TX Panhandle into southern KS including the Wichita area. Notably, PWAT has been measured at 1.50 to 1.60", suggesting a deep layer of boundary layer moisture coincident with the steep low-level lapse rates. Storms are already occurring over the northeast TX Panhandle and into far northwest OK, producing strong gusts. Outflow from this activity may push into KS, where a weak wind shift exists. Therefore, scattered storms are expected to develop into these areas, and locally severe gusts appear likely. Coverage of severe may not warrant a watch, but trends will continued to be monitored

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: Scattered strong to occasionally severe thunderstorms will bring an isolated risk for damaging/severe wind gusts through this afternoon

details.label: Summary
details.text: Scattered strong to occasionally severe thunderstorms will bring an isolated risk for damaging/severe wind gusts through this afternoon

details.label: Discussion
details.text: In the wake of morning cloud cover, strong diurnal heating and steepening low-level lapse rates amid low-to-mid 50s dewpoints are supporting scattered thunderstorm development within a corridor of greater buoyancy (500-1500 J/kg MLCAPE) across portions of the Great Basin and lower Colorado River Basin. Enhanced southwesterly flow downstream of an upper low centered off of the California coastline is contributing to modestly enhanced effective shear of 25-35 kts, sufficient for modest updraft organization. In conjunction with steep low-to-mid level lapse rates, high LCLs (2-3+ km), and inverted-V thermodynamic profiles, an isolated risk for damaging/severe wind gusts may accompany developing thunderstorms through this evening. This risk is expected to remain relatively isolated. Thus, watch issuance is not anticipated

details.label: Most probable threats
